subject: Throughput degradation impacting inference API - Novacorp
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novacorp.com>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@novacorp.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput degradation impacting inference API - Novacorp

Hi Elaine / Jake,

We’re seeing an elevated p95 and increased 5xx rate for Novacorp’s hosted inference endpoints in us-west-1 starting ~08:50 PDT. Our initial triage shows increased token queueing and higher-than-normal worker CPU utilization on the model pool serving your project.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Activated traffic fallback to a sibling pool to reduce request queuing
- Temporarily increased concurrency headroom for your project
- Enabled extended logging for affected requests (sampling)

Could you share any request patterns (batching, request sizes) or recent config changes on your side that might coincide with the start time? If you have sample request IDs, please attach them—our logs will be easier to correlate.

We’ll keep this thread for customer updates; Sean and Olga are on-call for infra/serving.

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll send a targeted status update within 30 minutes once we confirm mitigation.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: incident_runbook.pdf (incident checklist), novacorp_api_samples.log (requested if available)

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novacorp.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:23:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput degradation impacting inference API - Novacorp

Thanks for the quick note, Aisha — we’re seeing elevated latencies on our side as well. Our engineering team confirms there were no recent client-side config changes.

Impact: several production flows are hitting elevated p95 (~1.2s -> 3.8s) and a small percentage of 502s for batch generation calls between 08:50–09:10 PDT. We captured a few request IDs and attached the log snippet.

Attached: novacorp_sample_requests.txt (3 request IDs), internal error traces (redacted)

Please advise on ETA to steady state. We’re standing by and can provide additional traces if it helps.

—Elaine
VP Engineering, Novacorp

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:31:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput degradation impacting inference API - Novacorp

Aisha / Olga,

Quick findings from infra:
- There was a recent gradual rollout (04/12 08:30 PDT) of a batcher tuning change intended to reduce tail latency. The change increased max_batch_window_ms from 8 -> 12ms; under the Novacorp traffic distribution this appears to have increased batch formation latency and increased CPU due to more aggressive padding.
- Autoscaler behaved as expected but scaling lag combined with larger batches caused queuing and occasional worker saturation.

Proposed immediate remediation:
1) Roll back the batcher-tuning rollout for the Novacorp model pool (target: 10:00 PDT)
2) Keep fallback routing active while we validate
3) Collect targeted trace samples for the rollback window

I’ll prepare the rollback patch and coordinate with infra ops — Olga will run the rollback and monitor p95; Aisha please send a customer-facing note with ETA.

Sean
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novacorp.com>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@novacorp.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Update: Throughput degradation resolved — Novacorp incident INC-20270412

Hi Elaine / Jake,

Following up — we completed a targeted rollback of the batcher tuning change at 10:02 PDT on 4/12. Since the rollback we’ve observed your p95 latencies return to baseline (median p95 1.1s) and the 5xx rate has dropped to background levels.

What we did:
- Rolled back batcher max_batch_window_ms for your model pool
- Continued fallback routing until we verified stabilization
- Collected request traces and correlated them with the sample IDs you provided

Next steps:
- We’re drafting a concise postmortem and action items (link below). Expect an initial postmortem by EOD today. The postmortem will include a permanent mitigation plan: a canary gating rule for batcher parameter rollouts and a short-term increase in autoscaler sensitivity for affected pools.

Attachments: postmortem_draft.md
Status page incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270412-novacorp

Apologies again for the impact. If you’d like a short walk-through with engineering, we can schedule a 30-minute sync later this week.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
